original_question: In asymptotic parameter-estimation theory for finite-dimensional models on infinite sample spaces, can the usual regularity assumptions be reformulated as geometric conditions on the corresponding submanifolds of an infinite-dimensional manifold?
target_in_paper: Section 6 (Hiroshi Nagaoka), problem 1(b): the open problem asking whether the complicated regularity conditions used in the traditional asymptotic theory of parameter estimation for finite-dimensional statistical models on infinite sample spaces can be expressed as geometric conditions on those models when they are viewed as submanifolds of an infinite-dimensional manifold of probability distributions.
correct_elements: Your draft identifies the correct target almost exactly. It correctly singles out finite-dimensional statistical models on infinite sample spaces, places them inside an infinite-dimensional manifold, and asks whether the regularity conditions used in asymptotic parameter-estimation theory can be recast geometrically. That is essentially the wording of Section 6, problem 1(b).
missing_details: The paper explicitly frames the objects as finite-dimensional statistical models, not just arbitrary finite-dimensional models.

The ambient space is not an arbitrary infinite-dimensional manifold: in the surrounding context it is the infinite-dimensional manifold of probability distributions on infinite sample spaces, under whatever standing conditions are needed to make that geometry rigorous.
The motivation is not merely reformulation for its own sake; the paper asks whether this viewpoint helps us understand or simplify statistical discussions about such models.
The scope is specifically the traditional asymptotic theory of parameter estimation.

The note immediately following problem 1(b) stresses that parameter estimation should be kept conceptually distinct from large deviation and hypothesis-testing problems; a faithful restatement should preserve that focus.

The paper does not specify a particular list of regularity assumptions or a precise class of geometric conditions, so a stand-alone rewrite should remain open-ended rather than inserting assumptions such as LAN, DQM, smoothness orders, or identifiability criteria that the paper itself does not name.
refined_question: Let M be a finite-dimensional statistical model on an infinite sample space, viewed as a finite-dimensional submanifold of an infinite-dimensional manifold of probability distributions satisfying the standing conditions needed to make that ambient geometry rigorous. In the traditional asymptotic theory of parameter estimation for M, can the several complicated regularity conditions usually imposed on the model be reformulated as geometric conditions on the submanifold M, in a way that clarifies or simplifies the statistical theory, specifically on the parameter-estimation side rather than the large-deviation or hypothesis-testing side?
justification: The draft matches Section 6, problem 1(b) almost verbatim, so that is the nearest official formulation in the paper. It is narrower than Section 6, problem 1(a), which concerns Sanov's theorem, Cramer's theorem, and infinite-dimensional differential geometry, and different from Section 6, problem 2, which asks about autoparallel submanifolds of density operators. The only nearby clarification that materially sharpens the draft is the note following 1(b), where Nagaoka emphasizes that parameter estimation and large deviation or hypothesis testing are essentially different kinds of problems; this should therefore be reflected in the refined question. Because the paper does not enumerate the regularity assumptions or propose a specific geometric criterion, the rewrite should stay deliberately open-ended and should not introduce extra hypotheses absent from the paper.
